notes:
Here are my notes on Joshua 4, organised verse by verse. A few gaps first. I found nothing on bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org, newadvent.org or oca.org. I also found no prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching on this chapter, and no notes from Spurgeon, Lutheran or Pentecostal sources. Those parts are left out. Some sources give a Church Father's view second-hand, and I say so where that happens. A note on labels: none of the pages names its author's denomination. Where I give one (Calvin as Reformed, Gill as Baptist), that comes from my general knowledge, not from the pages.

## Part 1: The traditional reading, verse by verse

**v. 1:** The wording almost repeats Joshua 3:17. Precept Austin says the Spirit meant to stress that Israel was now in the Promised Land. It also notes that God gives Joshua his orders one step at a time. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
Guzik says the people had waited about 40 years for this moment. Crossing the Jordan was the final geographical barrier to the land of Canaan. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/

**v. 2:** The same order was given in 3:12, so the twelve men had probably been chosen already. Two and a half tribes would live east of the Jordan, yet one man still came from every tribe, a sign that the nation was one. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
GotQuestions counts the number twelve five times in vv. 1–8. It says this stresses the unity of the tribes as one nation under Joshua's leadership. https://www.gotquestions.org/stones-of-remembrance.html

**v. 3:** The stones came from where the priests stood with the ark. Guzik says each was undoubtedly a large stone. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
Setting up stones as a memorial happens often in the Old Testament (Gen 28; 1 Sam 7:12). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
The stones came from the middle of the river, not the shore. GotQuestions says this highlights that Israel crossed on dry land. https://www.gotquestions.org/stones-of-remembrance.html
The "place where you spend the night" was Gilgal. Sources disagree on how far it was from the river: Precept Austin says about 1.25 to 2 miles, while George Bush (19th century) says over six miles. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary

**v. 4:** Precept Austin says Joshua obeyed God at once. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
Guzik sees the twelve men as standing for all twelve tribes, so that the whole nation took part. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/

**v. 5:** The stones were carried on the shoulder, so they were fairly big. It fits that they came from where the ark stood, because the ark (the LORD) is why Israel could cross. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
Commentators read "cross over before the ark" in different ways:
- George Bush thinks the twelve were still behind the ark and now went ahead of it. He calls the idea that they walked back across a "violent construction." https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
- Coffman thinks the men did go back to where the priests stood, which shows the people were still crossing. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html

**vv. 6–7:** Guzik says the stones were a *sign* because of where they came from, and a *memorial* because they kept the event in mind. The crossing was the last miracle of the exodus journey: Israel left Egypt through parted water and entered Canaan the same way. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
He quotes the scholar Hess: later generations would "participate" in the crossing by seeing the sign and hearing it explained. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
Precept Austin links the passage to the children's questions at Passover (Ex 12:26–27; 13:14) and to Deuteronomy 6:20–24. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
On the repeated phrase "the waters were cut off": an older note on Precept Austin says the repetition marks how wonderful the miracle was. It reads "forever" as for as long as the nation lasted. It says the memorial was mainly for Israel, but also a warning to the nations around. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
A.W. Pink calls the pile a message to the heart through the eyes, an "enduring sermon in stone." https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
Another writer on Precept Austin compares the stones to the Lord's Supper: God gives visible symbols because he knows how much we are moved by what we can see. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary

**v. 8:** "The Israelites" did this through the twelve men, who acted for the whole people (George Bush). Precept Austin adds that the Jordan was still being held back while they obeyed. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
Matthew Henry says that by these stones God, as it were, handed Israel the legal deed to the land. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html

**v. 9:** Most say there were two memorials. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
- Guzik says the river stones could be seen in droughts, when the Jordan ran low. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
- Barnes thinks the priests stood near the eastern edge. Water would reach the stones only in flood time, so they could be seen and stay in place. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- Gill wonders whether these were the stones John the Baptist pointed to (Matt 3:9), since John baptised at Bethabara. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- Cyril Barber: the Gilgal memorial recalled *what* happened, and the river memorial recalled *where* it happened. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary

"To this day":
- Keil & Delitzsch take it to mean the time the account was written. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-10.html
- George Bush suggests either Joshua wrote it about 20 years later, or Samuel, Ezra or another inspired editor added it. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
- Gill holds that Joshua wrote it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html

**v. 10:** The priests stood with the ark for the whole crossing, as the visible sign of God's presence. The people may have hurried out of eagerness, or worry about when the water would return. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
Thomas Scott (quoted on Precept Austin): the priests stayed until Joshua told them to go, and Joshua waited until God told him. Every party obeyed God's word. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary

**vv. 11–13:** Guzik says the eastern tribes kept the promise they made in Joshua 1:12–16. They sent their armies to fight for the rest of the nation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
The Gospel Coalition commentary says the author stresses Joshua's leadership over *all* the tribes. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/joshua/
I found no comment on the 40,000 figure.

**v. 14:** God kept his promise of 3:7. Joshua becomes a "new Moses": after the Red Sea the people trusted Moses (Ex 14:31), and now Joshua is in a very similar place. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-4/
Matthew Henry says Joshua was honoured for Israel's sake, not his own. He adds that leaders earn respect through holiness and love, not threats. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_004.cfm

**vv. 15–17:** Precept Austin says obeying this command completed the miracle. It showed the event was supernatural, not a coincidence. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary

**v. 18:** Joseph Parker says God gave no way back. As soon as Israel crossed, the river returned and Israel was locked up to his work. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
Maclaren (quoted by Guzik): from now on the desert was as unreachable as Egypt. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/Joshua+4/
Fleming's Bridgeway Bible Commentary thinks God used natural means at the right moment. A collapse of the riverbanks at Adam dammed the river, and the water returned when that earth dam broke. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html

**v. 19:** The tenth day of the first month is when Passover lambs were chosen (Ex 12:3), so Israel entered Canaan on the anniversary of leaving Egypt. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/Joshua+4/
Chuck Smith notes it was four days before Passover. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-10.html

**v. 20:**
- Gilgal may mean "circle of stones." https://biblehub.com/joshua/4-20.htm
- Bible.org: "a rolling" or "a circle of stones." https://bible.org/seriespage/3-crossing-jordan-joshua-31-424
- Constable: the site has not been identified for certain. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- Gill notes that Josephus says Joshua built an altar from the stones, and that Tertullian placed them by the ark. Gill calls the second idea very unlikely. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/4-20.htm

**vv. 21–22:** Donald Campbell says a father was not to send his child to a Levite for answers but to answer himself. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
The Biblical Illustrator says "fathers" means parents, but warns fathers against leaving religious teaching to mothers. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-10.html
Calvin calls this a kind of solemn dedication of the monument. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-19.html

**v. 23:** God dried up the Jordan as he dried up the Red Sea. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
Guzik draws a contrast: at the Red Sea Israel went away from danger, but at the Jordan it went toward it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-3/
A commentator on Bible Hub says that since the Red Sea is called a "baptism into Moses," this could be called a baptism into Joshua. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/4-20.htm

**v. 24:** Guzik says the purpose reached the world too: people should know there is a God in heaven who works miracles. https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/guzik_david/study-guide/joshua/joshua-4.cfm
Matthew Henry says God's rescues are a fair warning to others not to fight against the Almighty. He adds that remembering should keep Israel from other gods and in God's service. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_004.cfm
Bible.org links this to Israel's calling as a nation of priests, and says Christians are "living stones." https://bible.org/seriespage/3-crossing-jordan-joshua-31-424

## Part 2: Where Protestant teachers differ

**v. 9, can a sunken memorial be any use?**
- Calvin (Reformed) grants that a buried monument would be useless in itself. But he says talking about it still strengthened faith, just as the hidden ark did. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- Constable says two piles gave the children and the Canaanites "two witnesses." https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- Bible.org (Utley) says the river pile must have been at the edge, or it would never be seen. https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-3

**vv. 9 and 20, the two piles as pictures of Christ:**
- Pink sees the two monuments as baptism and the Lord's Supper. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- Coffman (Churches of Christ) agrees, saying these two ordinances last "forever." https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-3.html
- J. Vernon McGee (dispensationalist): the stones in the river picture Christ's death, and those on the bank his resurrection. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary
- Macmillan calls the crossing a "baptism of repentance." For him the buried stones show the fate Israel deserved. https://biblehub.com/sermons/auth/macmillan/the_stones_buried_in_the_jordan.htm
- The Biblical Illustrator says that when a child is baptised it crosses from nature into grace. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-10.html

**What the Jordan and Canaan stand for (vv. 1, 18):**
- Matthew Henry: the believer's passage through death to heaven. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-3-commentary
- Wiersbe: entering our inheritance in Christ by faith, where victories still have to be won one by one. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-3-commentary
- McGee: the Jordan "speaks of sanctification." https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mcgee_j_vernon/eBooks/have-you-crossed-over-jordan.cfm
- A Holiness-movement writer (Berry) treats crossing into Canaan as entering "entire sanctification." https://biblehub.com/library/berry/adventures_in_the_land_of_canaan/chapter_two_the_crossing_of.htm

**vv. 6 and 21, used for revival:**
- Chuck Smith (Calvary Chapel) warns that revivals seldom reach a second generation. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- A sermon excerpt on Precept Austin applies "What mean these stones?" to the 1859 revival, which it sees as like Pentecost. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-4-commentary

## Part 3: Other views

**Catholic:** Catholic.com notes that some Fathers (Gregory and Augustine) saw the waters turning back as a picture of baptism. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/joshua
The Biblical Illustrator says Augustine read the two piles as the twelve patriarchs and the twelve apostles. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-10.html

**Modern critical scholarship, reported second-hand on older commentary sites:**
- The Pulpit Commentary names Meyer and Knobel, who see v. 9 as taken from a separate account that doesn't fit the rest. It also notes Rosenmüller's objection that nobody would build a monument in a fast river. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/4-9.htm
- Gaebelein quotes George Adam Smith as finding two accounts of the monument. Gaebelein replies that there were simply two acts. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/gab/joshua-4.html
- Kennicott wanted to change "in the midst" to "from the midst" in v. 9. Adam Clarke rejects this, because no manuscript supports it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- Hess and the NIV take it as one pile only. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- Constable points to Brian Peckham's article on how chapters 3–4 were put together. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/4-9.html
- A Bible Hub article links Adam Zertal's foot-shaped stone enclosures in the Jordan Valley with Gilgal. https://biblehub.com/q/Why_are_12_stones_in_Joshua_4_9_important.htm
